title: How does offstage route a command, or a cloud job, to somewhere off your screen?
audience: Engineers onboarding to offstage and offstage cloud
scope: Local `offstage run` across headless/container/session lanes, plus cloud tasks, sandboxes and agent runs on fleet Mac slots.
omissions: Billing, CI, maintenance and third-party internals

notes.title: Routing: lane choice and cloud dispatch
notes.text: classify() reads only argv and repo files: session > container > headless. A refuse signal (installer, .pkg/.dmg, hdiutil) blocks every lane, even with --lane. Cloud: POST /v1/tasks checks auth, GUI gate, capacity, credit; /claim serves sandboxes first, then team-fair tasks.

notes.title: State and result lifecycle
notes.text: Local: each run gets .offstage/runs/<id> and a best-effort result.json LaneResult. Cloud: state lives in memory and is written atomically (temp + rename) to /data/plane.json every 2 s when changed and on SIGTERM, so a crash can lose ~2 s of acknowledged writes.

notes.title: Failure, isolation and retry
notes.text: Lanes never throw or fall back to your screen: no substrate → skipped (exit 69). sessiond checks peer uid, refuses input on console. Cloud: an unstarted claim requeues after 20 s (3 tries); a box silent 2 min fails its running tasks, no rerun. Slots claim only behind a fail-closed pf guard.

views.title: How do offstage clients, the cloud plane and fleet execution connect?
views.scope: System context for cloud work. Local execution stays on your Mac (A); use the selector for the local and cloud workflow details.

notes.title: Choose a workflow in the selector
notes.text: A = local execution and artifacts. B = submit → claim → execute → reset. C = sandbox agent → model proxy. D = console sign-in → session API. Shared letters link steps across views.

notes.title: Deployment and failure context
notes.text: Fly hosts one plane in sjc, so it is a single point of failure. Fleet execution stays on Studio A. Plane state is memory plus /data snapshots; source review is not a live check.

views.title: How does offstage execute a command away from your screen?
views.scope: A = local execution. CLI/MCP selects one alternative lane; result persistence is in the next view.

notes.title: Refusal beats --lane
notes.text: An installer, .pkg/.dmg or hdiutil in argv is refused on every lane, no override; --lane headless can't downgrade a GUI verdict. Nothing runs; the result is errored.

notes.title: No fallback to your display
notes.text: No Docker or helper session → skipped, exit 69, never your screen. The container drops DISPLAY; sessiond checks peer uid and refuses input when on the console.

views.title: Where are local run results and artifacts stored?
views.scope: A2 follows local execution or refusal. Return to the first view for lane selection and isolation.

notes.title: One directory per run
notes.text: Each run gets .offstage/runs/<id>/. Lanes write logs and captures there; the CLI persists the normalized LaneResult once execution returns, including refusals.

notes.title: Result writes can fail
notes.text: A failed result.json write is reported by the CLI. A run directory is a local archive, not a remote database or a promise of replicated durability.

views.title: How does the plane admit cloud work and keep its state?
views.scope: B = cloud task; C = sandbox agent. Admission precedes fleet execution (next view); C continues in the agent proxy view.

notes.title: Admission before queueing
notes.text: POST /v1/tasks re-checks the caller after reading the body, then GUI gate, capacity, credit; a repeated idempotency key replays. GET ?wait= holds until the task ends.

notes.title: Acknowledged is not yet durable
notes.text: Writes are acked from memory; plane.json is rewritten atomically every 2 s if changed and on SIGTERM, so a crash can lose ~2 s of acked work.

views.title: How does a fleet box claim a task, run it in a slot, and wipe it?
views.scope: B2–B5 continue cloud task submission. C3/C6 reuse execution/reset for agents. Heartbeats run independently.

notes.title: Claims, heartbeats, requeue
notes.text: Claim long-polls ≤25 s. Unstarted 20 s after claim → requeue (max 3 tries); box silent 2 min → running task fails, not rerun. Heartbeat (15 s) delivers cancels.

notes.title: Guarded claim, reset before the next
notes.text: A slot claims only while the pf LAN guard checks out (fails closed). Before its next claim it is reset: processes killed, home wiped, account remade with a new uid.

views.title: How does a sandbox agent run reach Claude without the slot holding a key?
views.scope: C2–C6 continue sandbox admission. Slot → plane → Anthropic keeps the customer key out of the slot. B3/C3 and B5/C6 are shared steps.

notes.title: The key stays on the plane
notes.text: The customer's Anthropic key stays in plane memory for one run; the slot gets an omt_ token. The proxy checks model, step budget and max_tokens; no streaming.

notes.title: Op relay and answer retries
notes.text: Ops run concurrently as the slot user; each poll reports room. An answer is resent with backoff until the plane takes it, and gets one try once closing.

views.title: How does the console sign in and access cloud state?
views.scope: D = optional Clerk sign-in: D1 → D2 → D3 verifies the token; D4 uses the plane session. State snapshots are independent.

notes.title: Optional social sign-in
notes.text: When configured, GitHub/Google auth uses ClerkJS. Console exchanges the token at /v1/auth/clerk, then signs out of Clerk; subsequent API calls use the plane session.

notes.title: State and admission
notes.text: Plane state and artifacts live on /data. New email accounts cannot mint keys or run work before verification; GUI admission is separately gated.
